name: Speed Metal
about: Speed metal is the fast, clean-picked metal that sits between the NWOBHM and thrash: Motörhead's velocity and Judas Priest's twin-guitar precision pushed to the limit, but with melody, high vocals and song structure kept intact. Accept's Fast as a Shark in 1982 is usually called the first speed metal song, and Exciter, Anvil, Raven and Metallica's Kill 'Em All had made it a style by 1983. In Germany, Helloween, Running Wild and Blind Guardian turned it toward power metal; in Canada and California, Exciter, Razor and Agent Steel kept it raw. By the late 1980s thrash had absorbed most of its energy, with Judas Priest's Painkiller as a late summit, and today a revival led by Sweden's Enforcer keeps the style running.

artists.name: Accept
artists.why: Fast as a Shark started it

artists.name: Metallica
artists.why: Kill 'Em All, the bridge to thrash

artists.name: Helloween
artists.why: Hamburg speed that became power metal

albums.title: Stained Class
albums.why: Exciter opens the album with double-bass drumming and a riff faster than anything then on record, the single most important prototype for the style.

albums.title: Ace of Spades
albums.why: The album that taught metal to play at punk tempo without losing its swing; every speed metal band owns a copy.

albums.title: Restless and Wild
albums.why: Fast as a Shark, with its fake folk intro and Stefan Kaufmann's double kick, is the genre's first true song, and Udo Dirkschneider's rasp carries the rest.

albums.title: Metal on Metal
albums.why: Lips and Robb Reiner's Toronto band were faster than almost anyone in 1982, and this crude, catchy album was studied by Metallica, Anthrax and Slayer alike.

albums.title: Black Metal
albums.why: The Newcastle trio's second album is as much speed metal as anything else, barely in tune and hugely influential on the thrash that followed.

albums.title: Heavy Metal Maniac
albums.why: Dan Beehler singing from behind the drum kit, a raw Shrapnel Records production and a title track that defined the genre; the first album with speed metal written all over it.

albums.title: Kill 'Em All
albums.why: Before thrash was named, Metallica's debut was speed metal with Diamond Head riffs and Motörhead attitude, and Whiplash still sets the pace.

albums.title: All for One
albums.why: The Gallagher brothers' third album, produced by Michael Wagener and Udo Dirkschneider, is their tightest and the one the thrash generation knew best.

albums.title: Fistful of Metal
albums.why: Neil Turbin's shriek and Dan Spitz's leads on an album that is speed metal rather than thrash, rough but with Deathrider and Metal Thrashing Mad to show for it.

albums.title: Gates to Purgatory
albums.why: Before the pirate costumes, Rock'n'Rolf's Hamburg band played Satanic speed metal with Prisoner of Our Time, a German cult record.

albums.title: Ample Destruction
albums.why: Harry Conklin's operatic vocals over Colorado speed metal, an American answer to the NWOBHM that power metal fans treat as scripture.

albums.title: Walls of Jericho
albums.why: Kai Hansen singing and shredding on the album that fused speed metal with Maiden melody, the direct ancestor of European power metal.

albums.title: Skeptics Apocalypse
albums.why: John Cyriis's alien-conspiracy screams and Juan Garcia's riffs on the Los Angeles band's debut, speed metal at its most intense and most strange.

albums.title: Master of Disguise
albums.why: Christian Logue's Los Angeles band made one of the fastest melodic records of the year, prized by collectors for its guitar work and its sleeve.

albums.title: Evil Invaders
albums.why: Guelph, Ontario's Razor at their most savage, with Dave Carlo's riffs pushing speed metal to the edge of thrash on a Canadian underground classic.

albums.title: Hellish Crossfire
albums.why: Hamburg's Iron Angel bridge speed metal and the first German thrash on a debut the Teutonic underground still rates among its best.

albums.title: Long Live the Loud
albums.why: Exciter's third album keeps the velocity of the debut with cleaner production; Victims of Sacrifice and the title track are speed metal to the letter.

albums.title: Thundersteel
albums.why: Mark Reale rebuilt Riot around Tony Moore's high vocals and Bobby Jarzombek's drums, and the result is the definitive American speed-power record.

albums.title: Battalions of Fear
albums.why: Before the Tolkien choirs, Blind Guardian were a Helloween-style speed metal band, and Majesty and Guardian of the Blind show how good they already were.

albums.title: Blue Blood
albums.why: Yoshiki's drumming and Toshi's voice turned Japanese speed metal into a national phenomenon, with Kurenai and the title track among the style's great songs.

albums.title: Painkiller
albums.why: Scott Travis's drum intro and Rob Halford's scream on a late masterpiece that out-ran the thrash bands Priest had inspired, the genre's summit.

albums.title: Diamonds
albums.why: Olof Wikstrand's Swedish band revived early-1980s speed metal with total conviction, and Midnight Vice and Katana are revival songs that stand with the originals.

albums.title: Head of the Pack
albums.why: Toronto's Skull Fist play the Anvil and Exciter tradition with Zach Slaughter's high vocals and a sense of fun, a sign that Canada never really stopped.

albums.title: Darkness Remains
albums.why: The Ventura trio's second album is the tightest product of the American revival, NWOBHM-style speed with a bassist-vocalist in the Lemmy mould.
